title: Standard n-Simplex
content: Defines membership in the standard n-simplex as the conjunction of two affine constraints: every coordinate is nonnegative, and the coordinates sum to one. This represents the convex hull of the n+1 unit basis vectors in ℝⁿ⁺¹, viewed as functions Fin (n+1) → ℝ. Encoding `Δⁿ` as a predicate on `Fin (n+1) → ℝ` (rather than a Subtype) keeps the function space ambient and lets Mathlib's continuity, pi-topology, and Finset.sum machinery apply directly without a layer of subtype lifts.

title: Support of a Simplex Point
content: The support records exactly which faces v lies on: i ∈ supp(v) iff vᵢ > 0, equivalently i ∉ supp(v) iff vᵢ = 0 (since coordinates are nonnegative — the auxiliary lemma supp_le packages this). Geometrically, supp(v) is the index set of the smallest face containing v in its relative interior. This is the central data structure that makes the Sperner coloring well-typed: we restrict the candidate color of v to lie in supp(v), automatically inheriting the Sperner boundary condition from a structural fact about face containment.
mathContext: $\operatorname{supp}(v) = \{i \in \{0, \dots, n\} \mid v_i > 0\}$ — the carrier of the smallest face containing $v$ in its interior

title: Support is Always Nonempty
content: A simplex point cannot have zero support: if all coordinates were zero, their sum would be zero, contradicting Σvᵢ = 1. This trivial-looking lemma is what guarantees the Sperner coloring is total — every vertex receives a color drawn from a nonempty index set. The proof uses Finset.sum_eq_zero applied pointwise (each coordinate is zero by supp_le applied with the empty hypothesis), then linarith against the simplex sum constraint.

title: Key Coloring Lemma — Heart of the Proof
content: The mathematical core of the entire Sperner-Brouwer route. For any simplex self-map of Δⁿ, at every vertex v there exists at least one supported coordinate i where f does not strictly increase: fᵢ(v) ≤ vᵢ. Proof is by contradiction: if f strictly increased on every supported coordinate, and f ≥ 0 = v on every unsupported coordinate, then Σf > Σv would follow from Finset.sum_lt_sum, contradicting Σf = 1 = Σv. This is a pure pigeonhole-by-summation argument — no continuity, no compactness, no topology — proving that the Sperner coloring is well-defined for ANY simplex self-map, not just continuous ones. The witness for the strict inequality in Finset.sum_lt_sum is precisely the (nonempty) supp(v).
mathContext: $v, f(v) \in \Delta^n \implies \exists i \in \operatorname{supp}(v),\ f(v)_i \le v_i$. Proof: $\sum_i f(v)_i = 1 = \sum_i v_i$ forbids strict majorization on supp$(v)$ when $v \equiv 0$ on the complement.

title: Sperner Candidate Color Set
content: The candidate color set for vertex v is the intersection of two conditions: the coordinate must be in supp(v), AND f must not strictly increase there. The previous key lemma exactly says this intersection is nonempty for any v, fv ∈ Δⁿ. By construction, colorSet ⊆ supp, so any color drawn from this set automatically satisfies the Sperner boundary condition. This two-stage construction (candidate set, then minimum) is a clean way to package the coloring as a deterministic function of (v, fv), avoiding any reliance on classical choice for the witness.

title: The Sperner Coloring c(v) = min colorSet
content: The Sperner color is defined as the MINIMUM index in the candidate set (any extremal selection would work; the minimum keeps the function deterministic without invoking choice). Three properties drop out automatically: (1) c(v) ∈ supp(v) since colorSet ⊆ supp (spernerColor_in_supp); (2) f(v)_{c(v)} ≤ v_{c(v)} by membership (spernerColor_le); (3) the BOUNDARY CONDITION — if vⱼ = 0 then j ∉ supp(v), so c(v) ≠ j (spernerColor_ne_of_zero). Property (3) is precisely the input that abstract Sperner's lemma demands of an admissible coloring on a triangulation of Δⁿ. The wrapped form spernerColorMap and its boundary lemma spernerColorMap_boundary repackage this with the input shape required by the abstract Sperner machinery.
mathContext: $c(v) := \min\,\{i \in \operatorname{supp}(v) \mid f(v)_i \le v_i\}$. Boundary condition: $v_j = 0 \implies c(v) \ne j$ (vertex on face $j$ is not colored $j$).

title: Axiom: Grid Sperner → Panchromatic Tuple
content: The single remaining axiom packages three independently-formalized pieces: (a) the Nth Freudenthal grid triangulation of Δⁿ from sperner-ndim-mathlib-oq-01; (b) the proved Sperner boundary condition spernerColorMap_boundary; (c) the abstract Sperner's lemma from sperner-ndim-mathlib (0 axioms). Crucially, the AXIOM IS PANCHROMATIC, NOT NEAR-FIXED-POINT: it returns n+1 distinct grid vertices, one per color, with the per-color inequality at each, plus a coordinatewise diameter bound n/N. That choice eliminates a spurious Lipschitz hypothesis from the downstream argument: a near-fixed-point '∀ i, |f(x)ᵢ - xᵢ| ≤ ε' would force a Lipschitz factor when comparing f(x) to f(vᵢ) at each color-i vertex, while the panchromatic form never compares f at two distinct points.
mathContext: $\forall N>0,\ \exists v_0, \dots, v_n \in \Delta^n: f(v_i)_i \le (v_i)_i\ \text{ and }\ |v_i^l - v_j^l| \le \tfrac{n}{N}\ \forall i,j,l$

title: Δⁿ is Compact (closed subset of [0,1]ⁿ⁺¹)
content: Compactness of the standard simplex is built explicitly via IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset rather than appealing to a packaged lemma. Δⁿ is rewritten as the intersection of n+1 closed half-spaces {v | vᵢ ≥ 0} and one closed hyperplane {v | Σvᵢ = 1}, each closed because they are level sets of continuous functions (continuous_apply, continuous_finset_sum). The ambient [0,1]ⁿ⁺¹ is compact by isCompact_univ_pi + isCompact_Icc. The bound vᵢ ≤ 1 follows from Finset.single_le_sum: every coordinate is bounded by the sum, which equals 1. This self-contained proof of compactness avoids importing convex-polyhedron theory and exposes the elementary geometry directly.
relatedConcepts: closed level sets of continuous maps

title: Subsequence Extraction + Diameter Squeeze
content: The classical Bolzano-Weierstrass extraction is performed via IsCompact.tendsto_subseq on the FIRST vertices uₙ := vdata(N, 0). This gives a strictly monotone φ : ℕ → ℕ and a limit x* ∈ Δⁿ with v(φk, 0) → x*. The diameter bound n/(φ(k)+1) → 0 (since φ is monotone unbounded and the divisor → ∞) lets us SQUEEZE every other vertex v(φ(k), i) toward the same limit: |v(φk, i)_l - v(φk, 0)_l| ≤ n/(φk+1) → 0, so via squeeze_zero_norm and the triangle inequality v(φk, i)_l → x*_l pointwise. The trick `(h_diff.add_const (x l))` then rewrites v⁰ - x* + x* = v⁰ to combine the difference convergence with a constant. This is the part of the proof that absolutely requires panchromatic tuples — a single-near-fixed-point input would lose the per-vertex structure here.
mathContext: $v_{\varphi(k)}^0 \to x^* \text{ and } |v_{\varphi(k)}^i - v_{\varphi(k)}^0| \to 0 \implies v_{\varphi(k)}^i \to x^* \text{ for every } i$

title: Sum-Forcing: Inequalities → Equalities
content: The endgame is the most elegant step. By continuity, each per-color inequality f(v(φk, i))ᵢ ≤ v(φk, i)ᵢ passes to the limit via ge_of_tendsto (applied to the nonnegative gap vᵢᵢ - f(vᵢ)ᵢ), giving f(x*)ᵢ ≤ x*ᵢ for every i. Then the SUM TRICK forces pointwise equality: by contradiction assume strict inequality at some i; Finset.sum_lt_sum then gives Σf(x*) < Σx*, but both equal 1 (since x*, f(x*) ∈ Δⁿ) — contradiction. So all inequalities are equalities — f(x*) = x*. This sum-forcing replaces a squeeze-on-difference argument that the near-fixed-point formulation would require, and it is precisely WHY no Lipschitz hypothesis is needed. The technique is reusable: any time you have one-sided pointwise inequalities and a known sum equality, tightness is automatic.
mathContext: $f(x^*)_i \le x^*_i \text{ for all } i,\ \sum_i f(x^*)_i = \sum_i x^*_i = 1 \implies f(x^*)_i = x^*_i \text{ for all } i$

title: Brouwer's Fixed-Point Theorem on Δⁿ
content: The main theorem is a one-line composition: feed the panchromatic tuple axiom into the proved fixed-point extraction. This makes the dependency graph crystal clear — the entire result rests on exactly ONE axiom (sperner_panchromatic) plus the abstract Sperner machinery and the proved coloring construction. Compare with the algebraic-topology route in brouwer-fixed-point: that approach axiomatizes Singular Homology, here we axiomatize a concrete combinatorial fact about a grid coloring. Both are real assumptions, but the Sperner route reduces the assumption to a single combinatorial axiom about the Freudenthal triangulation rather than an abstract category-theoretic edifice.
